newsitem.title: MEXICO: Leftist politician seized in southern Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Leftist politician seized in southern Mexico.

text.p: Mexican authorities on Thursday arrested a popular leftist politician in the southern state of Oaxaca on embezzlement charges, but his party said he was seized illegally to ruin his electoral chances.

Alfredo Lopez Ramos, candidate of the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) in the July 6 race for the lower house of Congress, was accused by the Oaxaca state government of embezzling some $100,000 while mayor of the port city of Salina Cruz last September.

His daughter, Rocio Lopez Barrera, witnessed his arrest and told Reuters he was beaten up and bundled into an unmarked pick-up truck by undercover police in Salina Cruz, some 340 miles (540 km) southwest of Mexico City.

Before the state attorney general's office issued a statement detailing the charges, she and his party assumed he had been abducted by supporters of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).

"We condemn the kidnap and we denounce the attitude of the PRI for generating a climate of violence with the backing of the state government," local PRD leader Saul Vicente told a news conference in the state capital, Oaxaca.
On Monday, Lopez Ramos declared his candidacy for the PRD in the national elections for federal deputies, and local political analysts had said he stood a good chance of winning.
But two days later a judge in Salina Cruz issued the arrest warrant, the state attorney general's office said.

According to PRD Senator Hector Sanchez Lopez, the arrest follows weeks of threats, harrassment and attempts to bribe Lopez Ramos that he alleged was the work of the Oaxacan's rival, PRI candidate Antonio Estefan Garfias.
The PRD said it had previously warned Interior Minister Emilio Chauyffet of the threats against its candidate.
In a statement issued by his party late Thursday, Lopez Ramos denied the embezzlement charges, and said he would fight for his right to compete in the elections.
The PRI, which has ruled Mexico for 68 years, is expected to face a strong challenge nationwide in the July polls.
